description: Sclerotinia fruit rot is a fungal disease that affects many crops and vegetables. The fungus survives in soil as black structures called sclerotia and infects plants during cool and wet conditions, causing soft rot and plant collapse.
symptoms: Soft wet rot on stems or fruits
White cotton-like fungal growth on infected tissues
Black seed-like structures (sclerotia) forming on infected areas
Rotting of stems, fruits, bulbs, or roots
visual_symptoms: white fluffy mold on plant tissue
black hard sclerotia inside white fungal growth
soft watery rot on stems or fruits
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in soil as sclerotia for several years
Sclerotia germinate and produce small cup-like structures (apothecia)
Apothecia release spores that spread by wind
Spores infect plant tissues during wet conditions
Infected plants produce new sclerotia that return to the soil
impact: Major crop losses in vegetables and oilseed crops
cultural_control: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Remove crop debris from the field
biological_control: Use biological agents such as Coniothyrium minitans
Use beneficial fungi such as Trichoderma species
chemical_control: Use registered fungicides when disease pressure is high
Apply protective fungicides during favorable disease conditions
prevention: Avoid planting susceptible crops repeatedly in the same field
